title: a payload buffer was sized to the declared text length and then filled completely
object: the APP_TEXT payload, one g_try_malloc0 of exactly textLength bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a buffer sized for its payload and then consumed as a C string
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:wiretap/blf.c allocates `textLength + 1` and writes `text[apptextheader.textLength] = '\0';` (`grep -c` = 1). The form without the extra byte is at 87803328179^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102426, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x102416` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the request size measured on the x86-64 host build alone, and the two agree.

nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the allocation is zero-filled by g_try_malloc0, so it LOOKS terminated -- and then blf_read_bytes overwrites every one of those zero bytes with file content, which is what removes the terminator. A reader checking only the allocator call sees a NUL-filled buffer.
